newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria may hold referendum in mid-November - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algeria may hold referendum in mid-November - paper.

text.p: Algeria might hold a referendum to amend its constitution on November 14 or November 15, almost coinciding with the first anniversary of a presidential election last year, Algeria's Liberte daily paper reported on Monday.
President Liamine Zeroual, who has not yet fixed a date for the referendum, last week set up a task force headed by Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia to prepare for the poll.
Zeroual was elected last November 16 in the country's first multi-candidate presidential poll.
The referendum seeks popular backing for change in the constitution to ban the use of Islam as a political weapon and confirm the Moslem faith as the state religion in Algeria.

It is seen a milestone in Zeroual's drive to create a multi-party democracy after the North African country's first pluralist general election was cancelled in 1992 and plunged the country into violence. The authorities scrapped that poll because Islamic fundamentalists had taken an overwhelming lead.
The referendum will precede parliamentary elections promised within the first half of 1997 and local elections in the second half of next year.
An estimated 50,000 people have died in Algeria's violence pitting Moslem guerrillas against government forces.
